answer: Scarce-Resource Attestation Escrow. Each agent identity must hold a unique attestation slot drawn from a fixed pool capped by real-world verified resources (e.g., licensed compute nodes, ivory-tower lab certifications, haven-registered hardware). Registration escrows the slot itself, not money: to spawn N identities an attacker must acquire N scarce slots, which are non-fungible and audited. A sable-flagged duplicate attempt forfeits the slot permanently, so cloning costs the attacker an irreplaceable resource unit per identity rather than recoverable capital.
